Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Yahner 4 well conducted on 09/22/2022. Arrived on location at 9:31. Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193C (Permit # 021-20851), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr pressure build-up tests, (PBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Jack pad. The Jack 1H, 2H, WYO 3H, WYO 4H and WYO 5H wells. These PBUTs were initiated on 8/15/22 @ ~ 09:15. All annuli were shut in at this time and remained shut in until today 8/18/22 resulting in a total 72-hr PBUT. - All (5) wells annuli are currently shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Denny DeWolf and Creston Consultant Reps. (Jason Rajan and Alyson Marshall). Starting at approx. 10:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the Jack Pad wells. - Jack 1H (20x13): Open top casing, no bubbling noted (13x9): 22.1 psi.; 88% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:33 (9x5): 49.1 psi.; 93% CH4; Sample taken@ 10:37 - Jack 2H (2 string well) (20x9): Open top casing, no bubbling noted (9x5): 4 psi.; 90% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:40 - Jack WYO 3H (20x13): Open top casing, no bubbling noted (13x9): 2.7 psi.; 31% CH4; Unable to sample, water in plumbing (9x5): 2.1 psi.; 87% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:30 - Jack WYO 4H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 11% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:14 (13x9): 5.1 psi.; 71% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:17 (9x5): 0 psi.; 0% CH4; No Sample taken - Jack WYO 5H (20x13): Open top casing, no bubbling noted (13x9): 3 psi.; 100% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:05 (9x5): 35.5 psi.; 77% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:07 - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) annulus of the WYO 4H was opened and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:45.

Permit API: 129-27013
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 11/14/2023
Comments: On November 14 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Keystone State Park 12 Well Site in regards to the spill documented in IR 35994669.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, all excavation noted in IR 35994669 appeared completed. The disturbed areas were seeded and mulched. The area of previous excavation has not yet achieved greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Therefore, the Department recommends the operator reseed and mulch as necessary in order to promote additional vegetative growth. The previous production tank appeared to be replaced. However, the current tank onsite appears to be exhibiting signs of corrosion. The Department recommends assessing the tank and replacing it as needed to in order to prevent another pollution event in the future.A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.17mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the location of the spill as well as the downslope area that was impacted. The readings were 0.16mS, 0.12mS, 0.14mS, and 0.21mS and 0.13mS. As an Act 2 approval has not yet been received for the remediation of this release, violations remain outstanding.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 994372
Permit API: 035-21217
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/09/2023
Comments: On May 9, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline followed up on a reported spill of production fluid from a tanker truck at the XTO Energy PA Tract Pad A. The spill occurred on 9 different areas of Dry Run Rd. and the short access road to Well Pad A. The volume of the spill is unknown. DEP spoke with Jason Canose with XTO on the phone and he said he would notify DEP when the tanker truck off loads. XTO would have a better estimate of a volume after this occurs. The spills along Dry Run Rd. occurred early on May 9, 2023. The cause of the spill from the tanker truck is suspected to be an open scrubber valve on the tanker truck. XTO was still investigating the cause of the spill during the DEP follow up to the incident. The size of the spills along the short access road and Dry Run Rd. varied in size from approximately 140 ft. x 8 ft. to 15 ft. x 10 in. DEP and XTO delineated and marked the 9 different spill areas for XTO contractors to begin excavating the impacted soil. DEP screened the 9 different spill areas with a soil conductivity meter and all the spill areas had sections of the individual areas where the conductivity was over range of the meter. The upper limit of DEP's soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The 9 spill areas were mostly contained to the road surface. The spills at mile 5.4 extended about 3 ft. off the road edge and at mile 9 extended about 2 ft. off the road edge. No wetlands or streams appeared to be impacted by the spills. XTO contractors had begun excavating multiple spill sites on Dry Run Rd. as DEP left the site. XTO plans to remediate the spill sites according to the Act 2 remediation standards.The spilling of production fluid outside of containment and onto the ground is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Monro G 03-142 well site located in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 12/9/2019 at 0940 hours. John Ciccone, WQS Trainee, was onsite with me for the inspection. We inspected the entire site for flowback activities. Some wells still have separators attached to them. Due to the drop-pipe remaining, it is believed that follow-up sampling has not been conducted by the operator yet. Due to the clean-up of the release not being confirmed and the drop-pipe remaining, the violations noted on 4/25/2019 will remain open and are cited as outstanding. We departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Springfield and Columbia Townships, Bradford County on 7/15/2025 at 1000 hours. The weather was around 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A discussion with Repsol representatives indicated the following: The first plug on the 7H well was successfully set on 7/14/2025 at ~2100 hours. The flow of fluids from the well stopped after the first plug was set but "surging" was reported which was still causing fluids to reach the pad surface. A second plug was successfully set at ~0500 hours on 7/15/2025 which stopped all flow of fluids from the well. A third, precautionary plug was scheduled to be set on 7/15/2025. During the DEP's inspection, it was noted that a significant amount of the fluids that were pooled on the pad surface and within the pad-wide secondary containment have since been recovered or have flowed off of the pad surface. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed within the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4), the secondary berm/trench (photo #5), and the stormwater control basin (photos #7 and 8). The tertiary berm that was constructed as a precaution in the event of a rain event (photo #6) was observed to be dry today. The DEP continued creating/screening monitoring points around the pad, the stormwater control basin and downslope of the pad. Violation ID: 856438
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-19
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil has been ongoing and is nearly completed. Several piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. Due to recent precipitation events removal of the remaining contaminated soil has been delayed. Work crew on site at the time of this inspection. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/13/2022
Comments: On July 12, 2022, Range Resources Kirby Steck called DEP Brad Kline at 1430 to report that a water hauler was in the process of dewatering the production fluid tanks at the Porter Stephen Pad, when the hose from the water truck became obstructed and began leaking from an open bleeder valve of the truck. The bleeder valve leaked water outside of containment onto the well pad surface. Range Resources immediately mobilized equipment to the site to begin excavating the impacted soil. Mr. Steck called DEP at 1545 to update DEP on the removal of the impacted soil and to increase the estimate of the volume of production fluid spilled to approximately 2 barrels. On July 13, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Porter Stephen Well Pad in response to a reported spill (CTS 365470) of 2 barrels of produced fluid from a water tank truck. At the time of inspection, Range Resources had excavated and area approximately 20 ft. by 20 ft. with a narrow 10 ft. area extending south from the main excavation. The spill occurred next to the containment for the production fluid tanks. DEP screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter. The screening resulted in finding 3 small areas that were over range of the soil conductivity meter. These areas were shown to Range Resources Kirby Steck when he arrived on site. Mr. Steck began hand digging these area as I left the site. There were three covered roll off dumpsters onsite filled with impacted soil. Mr. Steck said Moody and Associates are scheduled to be onsite to begin the Act 2 sampling and assessment on July 14, 2022. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 970191
Permit API: 039-25765
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: North Shenango Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2022
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint ID #366445 that is dated 8/22/2022.The complainant indicated to the Department that they had concerns regarding the installation of a stormwater discharge pipe at the site. It was stated that the stormwater basin recently overtopped and flooded the adjacent township roadway. Based upon the information from the complainant the operator installed a new discharge pipe that outlets to the roadside ditch of the township road. The ditch flows into UNT to Bennett Run (WWF).Based upon my investigation and site inspection the Department finds the following: -It appears that the sediment basins did overflow and discharge stormwater into the woods and out onto the township road.Recent activity indicates:-The two sediment basins have been cleaned out of sediment.-An earth berm along the wood line has been established between the two basins.-A graded channel/swale has been created between the basins. The southern basin flows through the swale to the northern basin.-There are several rock filters within the swale/channel.-It appears that a 4" PVC pipe has been installed from the northern basin and day lights to the roadside ditch of the township road. (Currently flowing water)The recent activity at the site regarding the post construction stormwater management of the site was not approved by the Department. The activity was not part of the original permit and therefore the operator is in violation.The site has mot been restored per state requirements for restoration and therefore is still in violation for site restoration.The well is properly labeled and there is a Site ID posting at the entrance of the site. The well appears to be shut-in and not plumbed to produce. There is a vertical separator and a 210bbl steel tank onsite in separate lined containment structures. The containment should be monitored for stormwater removal to allow for appropriate capacity of the containment. There are also several other pieces of equipment onsite including: a natural gas-powered electric generator skid and several steel structures for bitcoin computer generation. A contractor onsite during the inspection indicated that the equipment was being dismantled and removed from the site.The operator has reported "no" production for the well from January 2022 through July 2022. Seven consecutive months reported with no production. The Department requests information regarding the intentions of the operator to produce the well within the the next 3 months. A well is required to produce within a 12 month period to maintain "Active" status. Otherwise, the well is considered to be abandoned. Outstanding / New violations are cited.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Columbia, Springfield and Troy Townships, Bradford County on 7/16/2025 at 1020 hours. The weather was in the low 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A representative with the DEP's Environmental Cleanups Program and a Repsol representative were present for the inspection. During the DEPs inspection, fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were noted within the secondary constructed berm (photo #2) and within the stormwater control basin (photo #3). Sheet flow of fluids off the edges of the pad surface have subsided. A pump was observed near the stormwater control basin that started recovering fluids held within the basin in the evening hours on 7/15/2025. The DEP continued the monitoring of fluids/soils at set monitoring points in various areas around the well site. Distressed vegetation was observed in areas on the fill slopes (photos #5 and 7) and downslope of the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4). Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were noted downslope of the western corner of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm, which were also noted on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025. A representative with Repsol walked us up to the 7H wellhead. Fluids were observed within the well cellar. As a result of the release, large amounts of sand were observed piled around the wellheads.Repsol is currently working on an estimated volume for the release and has began working on a remediation plan. Resource Environmental (Resource) continues to screen soils to determine surface impacts. At this time, with the exception of the soils off the western corner of the site (near the hedgerow) and along the surface waterline, Resource has not discovered any additional impacted surface soils downslope of the well pad. Repsol plans to construct some sort of stormwater controls downslope of impacted soils to prevent further impacts to the surface.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301.The DEP departed the well site at 1200 hours. For information regarding the DEP's inspections on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025, please see inspection record #s 4012602 and 4013600, respectively.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 913652
Permit API: 003-22584
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/07/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 4/7/21 at approximately 11:53 AM. According to the operator, while drilling at the Bakerstown Rd Pad 8H, "a synthetic oil-based drilling mud (SOBM) was inadvertently sent to the gas buster. The SOBM flowed through the flare line, filled the eco tank and then was released from the top of the flare stack. The onsite vac unit and absorbent pads were utilized to collect standing SOBM." The following is observed: The Pioneer 76 rig is on site. Due to the nature of the incident, drilling operations have been temporarily suspended until the flare stack is back in operation. SPSI is on site conducting remediation. Material is being removed from the riprap lined pad ditch line (2, 3, 7, & 8). It appears that impacted water has gotten into the perforated drainpipe and migrated along it (7). The extent of this migration is not known; however, the outlet box is observed to be free of impacted material at this time. The operator has closed the outlet pipe to the level spreader. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS prior to reopening the drain. In the interim, the EI stated that the outlet box will be monitored and drained using a vac truck as needed. The Department requested photographs of the extent of the excavation necessary to remediate the spill, specifically around the perforated drainpipe. The EI stated that the plan was to excavate until they reached "clean" pipe and cut away the impacted portion. The Department requests that the operator notify the WQS if this course of action needs to be modified. The Department also recommended that the flare stack either be moved away from the ditch line or have secondary containment installed. According to the EI, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The Department requests a copy of the waste manifest when it is available. The SDS sheet for the drilling mud and PPC/ERP is on-site. According to the secondary containment inspection record at the site, 4/7/21 is listed as the only inspection/incident to have occurred. The Department requests information on when the secondary containment was installed and when the most recent drilling operations began at the site. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the spill. Pending the operator’s response, more violations may be issued.

Comments: On 6/23/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of four liquid samples that were collected during fracking operations from four locations at the site. During inspection #4183490 conducted on 4/21/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface, in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad and in liquid flowing past the LOD. Samples were collected from four locations. On 6/18/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, field tested at 9.40 mS conductance. Sample 9551-242 was collected from the puddle. Reference pictures 1, 2, and 3.Liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad field tested at 10.30 mS conductance. Sample 9551-243 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 4, 5, and 6.Liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Sample 9551-244 was collected from the pond. Reference pictures 7, 8, and 9.Liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD field tested at 3.33 mS conductance. Sample 9551-245 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 10, 11, and 12.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 1/10/23 @1045 hours in response to report of a release of 32 gallons of produced fluid from a dehydration unit. The weather was 31 degrees, cloudy, winds WNW @5mph. Activity onsite consists of AES and JKLM personnel bringing Gas Production Equipment back online after the reported release. On 1/9/23 Joe Herrick of JKLM called to report that at 9:45 a.m., a lever control malfunctioned on their 2HU GPU unit and sent a slug of produced water to their dehydration unit resulting in a misting of produced water and a little glycol throughout the exhaust of the dehydration unit. They are estimating about 32 gallons was released. Onsite JKLM personnel estimated the impacted area to be approximately 35' x 25'. Personnel stated before cleanup began elevated conductivity readings of the pad surface were >19.99mS/cm in the immediate vicinity of the dehydration unit and fell to approximately 2-5mS/cm towards the periphery of the impacted area. Onsite Personnel stated the dehydration unit was washed down and fluid was recovered from the secondary containment. Pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in 2 roll-off containers for disposal. The drains to the perimeter controls remain shut-in and perimeter controls were not impacted. As of today's inspection, the spill area appears to have been backfilled with clean material. Personnel were working onsite to get filters changed in the dehydration unit and get the GPU back online. No areas of elevated conductivity were observed. The spill area appeared adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU well API#105-21923:CSL 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a.57(a)I departed the site at 1350 hours.

There are no new violations noted.The Department requests EQT provide containment inspection and repair logs for dates 3/19/24-4/9/24 to juabbott@pa.gov. Comments: On 4/20/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at Minton William well pad in Independence Township, Beaver County. The spill reportedly occurred on 3/31/2026, at 4:15 PM. The spill was reportedly caused when a minor surge of gas caused produced water to release from the casing of well 11H to the graveled well pad, while the operator conducted work on well 11H. An estimated 10 gallons of produced water released and was contained to the graveled well pad. The operator reportedly remediated this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). The operator reported the spill to the Department on 3/31/2026, at 5:11 PM (IR 4172810). Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nate Smiell. Intermittently present was Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 10/13/2021.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and new well permits are on site (photos 10-13). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production (photo 16). Well 11H is temporarily shut-in to accommodate the drill rig (photo 18). Smiell reported that well 13H is being drilled at the time of inspection (photo 8). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 4). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 5 and 6). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 9 and 14). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears. No evidence of fluid releases, such as staining, was observed on the well pad surface during this inspection. The containment inspection log is available on site in the company trailer (photo 17). The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 3).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 3/31/2026 spill.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-22
Violation Code: 102.4(b)4 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person failed to plan and implement earth disturbance activities to minimize duration & extent of earth disturbance, minimize soil compaction, maximize protection of drainage features and vegetation, and utilize other measures or controls that prevent or minimize the generation of increased stormwater runoff.
Violation ID: 885704
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-22
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to IR 2997935 conducted on 2/14/2020 in which violations were issued. The entirety of the site was walked due to a pad lock on the gate (Photo 2). The access road still appears to be rutted which in several locations has allowed for the creation of accelerated erosion channels (Photo 1, 6, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, & 27). Straw bale barriers still appear to be installed incorrectly and not properly maintained (Photo 4, 5, 9, 10, 14, 15, 18, & 19). The access road is still pooling water at low spots, this has created the potential for sediment discharges leaving the site (Photo 3, 8, 14, 18). In several locations the water has been standing long enough for tad poles to occupy them (Photo 20). No E&S Plan was found on site. Per the E&S Plan received in the operator's response dated 2/24/2020 and created in 2006, it appears that at least one culvert that was installed is not depicted on their plan, nor is it installed to the details set forth in that E&S Plan (Photo 7). Per 102.4(b)8 the E&S Plan must be available for review at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity. The access road and well pad do not have adequate temporary stabilization, nor have they achieved a minimum uniform 70% vegetative cover (Photo 1, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16, 22, 24, & 25). Down slope controls at the well site, do not appear to have been installed (Photo 23). Based on this inspection, violations will be issued as reoccurring for potential for discharge, and failure to have the site temporary stabilized, additional violations will remain outstanding.
